definition: Predatory means living by hunting and killing other animals for food.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word predatory. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know predatory should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The dragonfly nymph is the pond's most predatory insect, taking tadpoles twice its own length.
Carnivorous says only that an animal eats meat, while predatory adds that it catches and kills that meat itself.
Rapacious is stronger and more judgemental than predatory, suggesting greed that runs well past need.

Hunting names the activity of pursuing and killing prey, and any animal, or person, can spend one afternoon at it. Predatory describes what a creature is: an animal whose living depends on the hunt, a whole diet and way of life rather than an act.

Stalking names one hunter's method -- following prey slowly and silently before the strike. Predatory covers the whole way of life of living by the kill, whether the killer stalks, ambushes, or runs its prey down in the open.

A camera trap at a Kenyan waterhole records the same leopard on eleven nights.
On six of them it stalks, kills, and eats an impala or a warthog; on the others it hunts without success and goes hungry.
It never touches the carcasses the hyenas abandon nearby, and it eats no plant matter at all.
The keeper's notes sum the animal up in a single word: predatory.
An animal that stalks and kills live prey on six nights out of eleven, refuses carrion, and eats no plants lives by hunting, which is what predatory means.

In biology predatory means killing prey in order to eat it, while in ordinary use it accuses, as in predatory lending.

When wolves returned to Yellowstone in 1995, ecologists expected the elk herds simply to shrink.
The herds did fall, but the larger change was in behaviour: elk stopped lingering in the open river valleys and kept to cover, moving constantly.
Biologists call this the ecology of fear.
A predatory neighbour changes a landscape even on the days it kills nothing.
Willows and aspens, browsed almost to the ground for seventy years, grew back along the streams once the elk no longer dared to stand and feed.
Beavers returned to the new willow thickets, and their dams slowed and cooled the rivers themselves.
